newsitem.title: USA: US official sees risk from further jobless fall.
newsitem.headline: US official sees risk from further jobless fall.

text.p: A U.S. Treasury Department official Tuesday said the economy was doing "extremely well" but warned of the risks of aggressively pushing unemployment down further.

"Clearly there would be an element of unacceptable risk in aggressively pushing the unemployment rate ever lower without reference to the inflationary pressures that might eventually emerge," Treasury Assistant Secretary Joshua Gotbaum said.
He told the Treasury's Borrowing Advisory Committee that jobs growth so far this year in excess of 200,000 per month was unsustainable.

Noting that financial markets expect job growth to rebound to about 220,000 in October, Gotbaum said, "such rates of job growth can hardly be sustained indefinitely, since they are about double the rate of growth in the working-age population."
The government is scheduled to release October payrolls figures on Friday. On Wednesday, it releases provisional figures for economic growth in the third quarter.
Financial markets expect economic growth to have slowed sharply to about two percent in the third quarter from 4.7 percent in the second.
Gotbaum said such a slowdown would be "a positive development." Continued growth at or near the second quarter's pace would create more problems than it would solve, he said.
Much of the growth that is expected in the third quarter is likely to come from a buildup of inventories.
"This is not necessarily anything to be concerned about," Gotbaum said. "Nonetheless it bears watching."
He called Tuesday's news of a slowdown in the growth of employers' costs in the third quarter "quite favorable."
The Labor Department earlier reported that the Employment Cost Index rose 0.6 percent in the third quarter after a 0.8 percent rise in the second.
